title: Your UnEmbedding Matrix is Secretly a Feature Lens for Text Embeddings

problem.claim: Large language models perform suboptimally as off-the-shelf text embedding models on massive embedding benchmarks.

gap.claim: The cause of this embedding deficiency is not adequately understood.

contributions.claim: EmbedFilter is a linear transformation for refining LLM-derived text embeddings.
The unembedding matrix encodes a latent subspace that writes frequent tokens into embedding space.
Filtering this subspace reduces high-frequency-token influence and enables dimensionality reduction for embedding retrieval.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across multiple LLM backbones reportedly show improved zero-shot downstream performance with EmbedFilter.
The reported performance improvement persists with significantly reduced embedding dimensions.
The authors report that reduced dimensions lower index storage and speed up retrieval while preserving refined embedding quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs have strong zero-shot capabilities but underperform as general-purpose text embedding models.
The authors associate the deficiency with frequent, uninformative token directions and their suppression of nuanced semantics.
The unembedding matrix is described as encoding a subspace that writes frequent tokens into embedding space.
EmbedFilter removes the identified subspace from LLM-derived embeddings.
The authors report improved zero-shot performance, lower-dimensional embeddings, reduced storage, and faster retrieval.
